faq: Do you change anything in my store?
No. An audit is read-only. You get a report and decide what to act on. If you want the fixes made, we quote them as a separate order in writing.
What do you need for the audit?
Your store link, and for deeper checks a shop manager or administrator user created for us. We never need your passwords and you can remove us after the audit.
Will you place orders in my live store?
Only if you agree, and we refund them straight away. We can also walk through checkout up to the payment step and test payment on a staging copy instead.
Does the audit cover legal pages?
We check that privacy, returns and terms pages exist and are easy to find. We do not give legal advice, so ask a professional to review the wording.

desc:
Ecom Swift LLC delivers a WooCommerce store audit and review: a written report on speed, checkout, product pages, plugins, security and tracking, with each finding ranked by importance and explained in plain language.

## What is a WooCommerce store audit?

A WooCommerce store audit is a structured check of how your shop performs for shoppers and how it is built behind the scenes. The result is a report that tells you what is working, what is hurting sales or safety, and what to fix first. It is an assessment, not a rebuild, so nothing in your store changes while we review it.

## Why a review helps before you spend more

WooCommerce stores grow in layers. A theme from one year, a plugin added for a promotion, a payment option someone installed in a hurry. Over time these layers slow the site down, conflict with each other and leave settings that nobody remembers choosing.

Without a review, owners tend to guess. They redesign the home page when the real problem is a slow checkout, or buy a new plugin when an existing one already covers the need. An audit replaces guessing with a ranked list, so your time and budget go to the issues that matter most.

## How an audit affects results

A shopper moves through a short chain: a page loads, a product looks believable, the cart is clear, checkout works. A weak link anywhere in that chain ends the visit. Slow mobile pages, a confusing shipping step or a broken coupon field all look small to the owner and decisive to the customer.

Security and tracking matter in a quieter way. An outdated plugin can expose customer data, and a broken analytics setup means you cannot tell which pages or campaigns bring buyers. Finding these problems early protects the business and gives you honest numbers to decide with. What you gain depends on how many of the fixes you then apply.

## What a thorough audit covers

- Page speed and mobile behavior on the home page, a category page, a product page and the cart.
- The full checkout path, including guest checkout, form fields, shipping choices and payment options.
- Active and inactive plugins, plus the theme, checked for age, overlap and likely slowdowns.
- Security settings such as user roles, login protection, update status and backups.
- Product page quality: photos, titles, variation selectors, delivery and returns details.
- Cart behavior, coupons and shipping calculations.
- Tracking: whether purchases, add-to-cart events and sources are recorded correctly.
- Search basics and product data, such as titles, descriptions and category structure.
- Findings ranked by importance, each with the reason it matters and a way to fix it.

## How we work

We review the store as a shopper first, on a phone and on a desktop, and then look at the technical side with read-only access. We take notes as we go and group findings by theme. Each item in the report gets a priority, a short explanation of the effect on customers or the business, and a suggested fix.

The Basic package gives you a health check of speed, checkout and plugins as a PDF report. Standard adds the security review, a look at product pages and the cart, and a video call where we explain the top fixes. Premium goes further with tracking and search checks, a three-month fix roadmap, a longer call and a re-check of the top fixes once you have applied them.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Fix the highest ranked items first, even if lower ones look easier.
- Keep a record of what you change and when, so cause and effect stay clear.
- Take a full backup before applying any fix from the report.
- Ask questions on the call if a finding is unclear.

**Avoid:**
- Treating every finding as equally urgent.
- Installing several new plugins at once to fix problems one by one.
- Ignoring security findings because the store seems to run fine.
- Applying changes straight to the live shop without testing.

## Who this is for

An audit suits an owner whose sales have flattened and who does not know why. It suits a buyer who is about to purchase an existing WooCommerce store and wants an honest view of its condition. It also suits a store that has had several different developers and needs one clear picture of the current state.

## What we need from you

Send the store address and tell us your main goal, such as faster pages or fewer abandoned carts. We ask for a read-only or limited user account, added as a team member, so we never need your password. We review the live store without placing real orders. If you want a test purchase checked, we will ask you first.
